function.name: select
function.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT
  url,
  title,
  published_at,
  UNNEST(
    SEM_EXTRACT_ALL(
      content,
      'a documented real-world incident in which a motor-vehicle driver followed GPS or satellite-navigation directions into a lake or other body of water, into remote desert terrain, or over/toward a cliff or precipice',
      incident_date := 'date the incident occurred, YYYY-MM-DD when available, otherwise YYYY-MM or YYYY',
      place := 'specific incident location, including city or landmark, region, and country',
      hazard := 'hazard category: lake or water, desert, or cliff',
      outcome := 'what happened to the vehicle and occupants, including deaths, injuries, rescue, or survival',
      gps_role := 'how the source says GPS or satellite-navigation directions contributed',
      victims := 'names of driver or occupants when stated',
      evidence := 'per_field'
    ),
    recursive := true
  )
FROM WEB_SEARCH(
  '"death by GPS" incidents lake desert cliff',
  'driver followed GPS into lake incident',
  'sat nav directed driver over cliff incident',
  'family stranded desert GPS directions rescue',
  'car drove into water following GPS news',
  'GPS navigation wrong turn remote desert death',
  'driver follows GPS off cliff news',
  'GPS led tourists into desert stranded'
)
WHERE SEM_MATCH(
  content,
  'documents a specific real incident involving a motor-vehicle driver following GPS or sat-nav toward or into a lake/body of water, remote desert, or cliff/precipice'
)","show_preview":false}

function.name: select
function.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT
  url,
  title,
  UNNEST(
    SEM_EXTRACT_ALL(
      content,
      'each distinct documented incident in which occupants of a road vehicle followed GPS or sat-nav directions and then entered a body of water, became stranded or died in remote desert terrain, or drove over/was directed toward a cliff or precipice; exclude walking, aviation, ordinary bridge crashes without a GPS link, and fictional stories',
      incident_date := 'date the incident happened, YYYY-MM-DD if stated, otherwise YYYY-MM or YYYY',
      location := 'incident location, with municipality or landmark, state/province/region, and country when stated',
      hazard := 'one of: water, desert, cliff',
      outcome := 'vehicle and occupant outcome, including number killed, injured, rescued, or unharmed',
      people := 'names or description of driver and occupants',
      navigation := 'GPS device, app, or sat-nav named and the navigation error or instruction',
      evidence := 'per_field'
    ),
    recursive := true
  )
FROM r9a9e5c575c1
WHERE SEM_MATCH(
  content,
  'the page provides factual details about one or more specific motor-vehicle GPS incidents involving water, remote desert, or a cliff, rather than merely generic safety advice or fiction'
)","show_preview":false}

function.name: select
function.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT
  SEM_NORM(
    COALESCE(incident_date, '') || ' | ' || COALESCE(location, ''),
    'merge rows that describe the same incident despite date precision or place-name wording; keep separate incidents at the same place on different dates'
  ) AS incident_key,
  ANY_VALUE(incident_date) AS incident_date,
  ANY_VALUE(location) AS location,
  ANY_VALUE(people) AS people,
  ANY_VALUE(navigation) AS navigation,
  ANY_VALUE(outcome) AS outcome,
  COUNT(DISTINCT url) AS source_count,
  ARG_MAX(url, LENGTH(COALESCE(outcome, '')) + LENGTH(COALESCE(navigation, ''))) AS url,
  ARG_MAX(title, LENGTH(COALESCE(outcome, '')) + LENGTH(COALESCE(navigation, ''))) AS title
FROM rf917b9be2b3
WHERE incident_date IS NOT NULL
  AND location IS NOT NULL
  AND navigation IS NOT NULL
  AND SEM_MATCH(
    COALESCE(incident_date, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(location, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(people, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(navigation, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(outcome, ''),
    'this is one specific real incident where a road-vehicle driver followed GPS or sat-nav and entered a lake or other body of water, was stranded/lost in remote desert terrain, or drove over/was directed toward a cliff or precipice; exclude bridges unless the vehicle entered water or fell from a precipice, snow or forest incidents without desert/cliff/water, pedestrians, boats, fiction, and generic discussion'
  )
GROUP BY SEM_NORM(
  COALESCE(incident_date, '') || ' | ' || COALESCE(location, ''),
  'merge rows that describe the same incident despite date precision or place-name wording; keep separate incidents at the same place on different dates'
)
ORDER BY incident_date","show_preview":false}

function.name: select
function.arguments:
{"query":"WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT
    incident_date,
    location,
    people,
    outcome,
    gps_role AS navigation,
    'water' AS category,
    fatalities,
    url,
    title
  FROM r847b632473c

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    incident_date,
    location,
    people,
    outcome,
    gps_role AS navigation,
    'desert' AS category,
    fatalities,
    url,
    title
  FROM r36f669a394e

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    incident_date,
    location,
    people,
    outcome,
    gps_role AS navigation,
    'cliff' AS category,
    fatalities,
    url,
    title
  FROM r335a12bae0c

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    incident_date,
    location,
    people,
    outcome,
    navigation,
    SEM_EXTRACT(
      COALESCE(location, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(navigation, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(outcome, ''),
      'hazard category for this incident; return exactly water, desert, or cliff'
    ) AS category,
    NULL AS fatalities,
    url,
    title
  FROM rf917b9be2b3
),
filtered AS (
  SELECT
    incident_date,
    location,
    people,
    outcome,
    navigation,
    lower(category) AS category,
    fatalities,
    url,
    title
  FROM candidates
  WHERE incident_date IS NOT NULL
    AND location IS NOT NULL
    AND SEM_MATCH(
      COALESCE(incident_date, '') || ' ' ||
      COALESCE(location, '') || ' ' ||
      COALESCE(people, '') || ' ' ||
      COALESCE(navigation, '') || ' ' ||
      COALESCE(outcome, '') || ' ' ||
      COALESCE(title, ''),
      'a specific, factual road-motor-vehicle incident in which the driver followed GPS, Google Maps, Waze, or sat-nav and the vehicle entered or approached a body of water, occupants became stranded or died in remote desert terrain, or the vehicle went over or became stranded at a cliff, ravine, precipice, or steep drop; include rescues and nonfatal cases; exclude pedestrians, boats, aircraft, fiction, jokes, generic warnings, snow-only and forest-only strandings, ordinary crashes with no navigation link, and stories where GPS was used only by rescuers'
    )
),
deduped AS (
  SELECT
    ARG_MAX(incident_date,
      CASE
        WHEN regexp_matches(incident_date, '^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$') THEN 3
        WHEN regexp_matches(incident_date, '^\\d{4}-\\d{2}$') THEN 2
        WHEN regexp_matches(incident_date, '^\\d{4}$') THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS incident_date,
    ARG_MAX(location, LENGTH(COALESCE(location, ''))) AS location,
    ARG_MAX(people, LENGTH(COALESCE(people, ''))) AS people,
    ARG_MAX(navigation, LENGTH(COALESCE(navigation, ''))) AS navigation,
    ARG_MAX(outcome, LENGTH(COALESCE(outcome, ''))) AS outcome,
    MODE(category) AS category,
    MAX(TRY_CAST(fatalities AS INTEGER)) AS fatalities,
    COUNT(DISTINCT url) AS corroborating_pages,
    ARG_MAX(url,
      LENGTH(COALESCE(outcome, '')) +
      LENGTH(COALESCE(navigation, '')) +
      LENGTH(COALESCE(people, ''))
    ) AS url,
    ARG_MAX(title,
      LENGTH(COALESCE(outcome, '')) +
      LENGTH(COALESCE(navigation, '')) +
      LENGTH(COALESCE(people, ''))
    ) AS source_title
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY SEM_NORM(
    COALESCE(incident_date, '') || ' | ' ||
    COALESCE(location, '') || ' | ' ||
    COALESCE(people, ''),
    'canonical incident identity: merge reports of the same event despite date precision, translated or abbreviated place names, and generic versus named occupants; keep genuinely separate events distinct'
  )
)
SELECT
  incident_date,
  location,
  category,
  people,
  navigation,
  outcome,
  fatalities,
  corroborating_pages,
  url,
  source_title,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS documented_incidents_in_scan,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS incidents_in_category
FROM deduped
WHERE category IN ('water', 'desert', 'cliff')
ORDER BY incident_date, location","show_preview":false}

function.arguments: {"brief":"Question asked verbatim: “Map every documented case of a driver following GPS into a lake, desert, or cliff — 'death by GPS' incidents”. Finding: this broad live-web scan found 103 distinct reported incidents after semantic filtering and incident-level deduplication: 59 water cases, 25 desert cases, and 19 cliff/precipice cases. These include fatal events, survivals, rescues, and near-disasters; “death by GPS” is used as the established umbrella term and does not imply every case was fatal. Present this as a documented-web census, not a provably exhaustive global registry: news coverage is uneven, some dates are only month/year or relative wording, precise coordinates were not published in the shaped data, and some incidents have only one accessible source. Make the methodology and these caveats prominent.\n\nUse r22b11ec5c08 as the core dataset: one row per deduplicated incident, with incident date, named location, category, people, GPS/navigation role, outcome, fatalities when extractable, number of corroborating pages, source URL and source title. It also carries repeated total and per-category counts. Lead with one large, beautiful world map using the named locations, geocoding/positioning them as accurately as the report renderer can from the location strings; cluster overlapping markers and color them distinctly: water blue, desert amber, cliff crimson. If exact coordinate plotting is unavailable, use a geographically organized map-like visual and explicitly label it approximate—do not invent precise coordinates. Emphasize the geographic spread and category imbalance (water is the majority). Follow with a timeline, category summary, and a searchable incident ledger. In the ledger, preserve blank cells rather than guessing missing values, link each row to its source, visually distinguish fatalities from rescues/survivals, and show corroborating-pages count as a confidence cue. Treat relative or malformed date strings as unresolved rather than placing them falsely on a precise timeline. Ask for a polished investigative-journalism visual style, readable on mobile, with clear legends and transparent sourcing. The scan was conducted 2026-08-31 across broad water/desert/cliff searches and multiple source types; underlying extraction considered hundreds of candidate reports before filtering and deduplication.","result_set_ids":["r22b11ec5c08"],"title":"Death by GPS: Documented Water, Desert & Cliff Incidents","prev_report_token":null}
